parsed.rationale: Although both `PlaybackController` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` live in the same package (`Playback`) and share a handful of members (`installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`, `play:`, `stop:`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and null Jaccard similarity, indicating the pipeline found no statistically significant overlap. More importantly, the two protocols encode distinct domain responsibilities: `PlaybackController` models high-level playback control with `PlaybackReason`-parameterised `play`/`stop`/`toggle`, `PlaybackState`, and loading state, while `TimeShiftablePlayer` models a lower-level, time-shiftable audio player with `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, and multiple async streams (`stateStream`, `timePositionStream`, `eventStream`). Forcing a parent–child inheritance relationship would either leak time-shift concerns into the general controller abstraction or create an artificially thin parent that adds no real reuse. The overlapping members (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `makeAudioBufferStream`) could at most be extracted into a narrow `AudioTappable` or `AudioBufferProducing` protocol, but that is a separate, smaller refactor not implied by this cluster.
